title: Ibn al-Qabāqibī to the compiler of a Mamluk book of cipher verses, about 1330-1370 (Penn LJS 51, f. 106v)

documents.shelfmark: University of Pennsylvania, Kislak Center, LJS 51, f. 106v (OPenn image 0084_0217)
documents.date: text about 1330-1370 (this project's survey); Penn dates the manuscript "14--" and gives no date for the text

plaintext.source: Red Arabic letters over the first five signs of line 1 only. The compiler's plaintext followed on a leaf that is lost.

transcription.source: OPenn master TIFF 0084_0217.tif, 2339 x 2959 px, read from line crops at 1.3x, 2.5x and 4x
transcription.notes: The catalogue entry estimated 120-130 signs; the measured count is 89. Two signs in line 1 are abraded and three signs of line 2 stand in a damaged patch. The pairs D/R and A/Q are close in shape.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic substitution of 22 invented signs for Arabic letters, right to left, with a dotted vertical stroke between words and one sign for lam-alif.
system.notes: Final alif maqsura written as alif; no hamza. Key order not established: the signs were not compared with an alphabet table.

prior_solution.where: No surviving or modern decipherment found; the compiler's own solution is lost with the leaf that followed (his remark says he solved it). The second of the two verses is a known verse: Ibn al-ʿAdīm, Bughyat al-ṭalab, under al-Agharr ibn Sinān al-Ḥalabī (found after the reading, not used). The text is placed by this project's survey at about 1330-1370; Penn dates the manuscript "14--" and gives no date for the text. Catalogue vetting of 15 Nov 2026 found no study or reading (Penn TEI, Digital Scriptorium, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry's list, web); two exact-phrase web searches for the verses on 16 Nov 2026 found nothing. Not searched: al-Qalqashandi (Subh al-a'sha, vol. 9), Arabic Origins of Cryptology.

conditions.human_role: The user gave the address of the catalogue's solve page for no. 2882 and asked for the cipher to be solved. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched the master TIFF of f. 106v from OPenn by plain curl and cut line crops.
Transcribed the seven lines sign by sign from the crops; about 35 shapes on the first pass.
Read the red letters over the first five signs as waw nun alif ayn sin; with the sixth sign as ta marbuta the first word is wa-na'isa.
The group of four signs ending alif-nun recurs three times, once followed by ha-alif: ajfan, wa-ajfani, wa-ajfanuha. Gave jim, fa, ha and the lam-alif sign.
Took the damaged word at the end of line 2 as jahannam and the next as a four-letter word in h-j.
Scanned line 1 as a tawil hemistich (qad ja'ala l-hawa) and used the metre to fix the second hemistich: laha muhjati mathwa wa-khaddi laha arda.
Read the triangle-bar-loop sign of lines 4 and 7 as ayn (a'ta, mu'ta).
Separated that sign from ayn as ra: arda, sahirtu, marda; wa-lam anam, wa-namat wa-lam tashad gave mim, ta, dal.
Read the last open word, four signs in line 5, as sihah from sense and metre; merged the shapes to 22 signs, all with values.

Viewed ff. 105r-106r: other writers, other alphabets, each with its plaintext; f. 106r has the compiler's remark on another message that lam-alif was made one letter. No alphabet was compared sign by sign.
Two exact-phrase web searches for the two verses.
Checked that all four hemistichs scan as tawil, that both verses rhyme in -da, and that the key is one-to-one over 22 signs.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 89 tokens, 22 types, ar-mamluk order 4: reading -2.537 per letter; random keys -4.901 (z 5.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.745 (mean -2.881, z 3.4); annealer on the real text -2.799. Verdict: pass.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Transcribed the seven cipher lines independently from the master TIFF (90 signs, 25 labels, 22 words) and checked the segmentation on connected components of the ink. Compared by position on 16 Nov 2026 with this folder's transcription: sign counts agree on six of seven lines, and its labels coincide with this folder's signs at 77 of 85 aligned positions.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Annealing over one-to-one keys, both directions, with the new ar-classical-poetry 5-gram model (788,143 verses); with and without the red-gloss values fixed. No sense; fixing the gloss values (read ta and ghayn at two positions) made the score worse.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): With only the commonest sign fixed as alif, read the two words sharing six signs as wa-amthaluka / wa-amthaluha. Of the ten signs it called firm, the alif and waw and three more match this folder's key (37 of 63 aligned positions); five (mim, tha, lam, ya, kaf) are wrong.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Homophones for lam and ha, then an alif sign that also stands for lam (from the compiler's remark that the writer 'made the lam alif'). The accepted key is one-to-one over 22 signs; that sign is alif only.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Scanned both lines as tawil with a rhyme in -da, and showed bayt 1 scans in full under its skeleton; bayt 2 was a syllable too long. Metre and rhyme class agree with the accepted reading (which has r for its y before the rhyme letter).

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Tested lam-alif as one sign (the compiler's stock formula): no sign took it in the solver, because the one sign that is lam-alif (rubbed, line 1) had been read as alif. Divider moves and one null alif were also tried.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Metre-constrained search (scansearch.py): syllable weights from 87,421 vowelled forms joined against the tawil hemistich. It recovers 'huma kanu wa-ma kulluha ayda' for one half-line, a reading that is not the accepted one; over 100,000 readings of the opening half scan, so the metre cannot fix the single-use signs.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Read the whole volume (images 0006-0217) for the circle's tricks and the sender's other ciphers; re-read the sender's name at 5x as Ibn al-Qubabi (or al-Qabbani), not Ibn al-Qaysarani. Not reconciled with this folder, which took the name from the sweep.

ljs51 attack (separate ciphertext-only session, kept as the record in targets/ljs51/): Outcome of the attack: no reading, outcome not solved. Compared with the accepted key on 16 Nov 2026: same glyph inventory and the tawil metre found; letters of the common signs found; most mid-frequency signs and the sense wrong.

ljs51 attack (separate record): on integration, found that the attack's Arabic normaliser (lm.norm arabic28) turned vowel signs into spaces, splitting the vowelled verses of its corpus; fixed in lang/lm.py on main. The attack's runs predate the fix and were not rerun, so its failure is that of the search as run.

Independent review for the second maintainer (issue #714): transcription checked against the repository crop, all four hemistichs scanned, an exhaustive word-list search found 21,037 one-to-one keys keeping the red gloss and making all 21 words attested forms, and 12 of 22 signs are forced; seven signs rest on one word each. Statistical test judged inconclusive at 89 signs. Reading holds, grade B.

Alan Elbaum (Princeton Geniza Project) sent eight corrections by email; each checked on the OPenn master TIFF at 2x-3x: sender's name ابن القباقبي; the compiler's remark with بحضوره; a supralinear alif before the lam-alif sign; extra letters in the damaged word of line 2; تسهر for تسهد (last sign of line 6 is R); red gloss و ت ا ع س; the ع of جعل and the last ح of صحاح are regular.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.537; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.799; seed sensitivity (16 Nov 2026): seeds 2, 3, 4 gave weak (shuffled-refit z 2.7), pass (5.7), pass (6.3), and in all four runs the reading scored above every shuffled refit; negative control (--control) underdetermined, z 0.5. Model ar-mamluk (lang/): 2.17 M letters of al-Hilli, Ibn Nubata, al-Safadi and al-Umari, OpenITI.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The entry was a red gloss over the first five signs of the cipher (five letters); the other 17 signs were recovered from repeated words, the tawil metre and the rhyme. No plaintext of the message survives and no reading was found.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt decoded with key.json (decode.py): 86 of the 89 transcribed cipher signs are read; the three signs of the damaged word of line 2 are not read, and at least two more signs stand there untranscribed (Elbaum, 23 Nov 2026); unit cipher signs
outcome.notes: Corrected 23 Nov 2026 after eight corrections from Alan Elbaum, each checked on the master TIFF (NOTES.md): sender Ibn al-Qabāqibī, not Ibn al-Qaysarani; red gloss و ت ا ع س (the second letter does not match the sign's value ن, which rests on the word); تسهر not تسهد; صحاح stands as written; a supralinear alif before the lam-alif sign; the first word of the second hemistich (read لها) is unread. Grades count doubtful signs only: C the four glossed signs whose gloss agrees with the key, M the damaged last sign of line 6, I two signs read from the word (O, J). The other signs are read from the recovered key and are not graded. Statistical validation with ar-mamluk (16 Nov 2026) gives verdict pass but is inconclusive at this length; it passes at the standard seed with narrow margins and is inconclusive at 89 signs (one weak run in four; the annealer cannot find the reading by itself), so it is not listed under verification; the reading rests on the metre, rhyme, grammar and the red gloss (Dudout, issue #714). Seven of the 22 signs rest on one word each.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), review for Brice Dudout (issue #714); a model's review, not a person's
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against translation_en.md: two complete tawil verses, all four hemistichs scanned foot by foot with no deviation beyond qabd, rhyme -rda in both; grammar and the sihah/marda antithesis hold. Transcription checked against docs/qaysarani1350_cipher.jpg (master TIFF not obtainable that day). Seven signs rest on one word each; sihah is written sihaj on the page and the first laha of line 2 is damaged, both marked in reading.md. Prior publication in al-Qalqashandi and Arabic Origins of Cryptology not checked. Replaces the grade A recorded by the authoring session, which is not an independent review.

texts.summary: Two love verses in the tawil metre sent in cipher by Ibn al-Qabāqibī to the compiler of the volume: love has made the poet's heart the dwelling of a drowsy-eyed girl and his cheek the ground beneath her; he lies awake with sound eyelids while she sleeps with 'sick' ones. One damaged word of the first verse is not read. The second verse is quoted by Ibn al-ʿAdīm under an earlier poet. The compiler's own solution was on a leaf now lost.

credits.note: Eight corrections to the page by email, 23 Nov 2026: the sender's name, the compiler's remark, the red gloss, تسهر, and four points of transcription.
